scope: The session revocation of a signing rotation, on a disposable pinned database with the pinned Auth's own schema: tenant triggers on the Auth tables ran as the superuser before and escalated; as the Auth login they are refused, held rows and lifted bounds make it give up, and nothing waits unbounded. Not a full rotation and not a running installation.

checks.check: host headroom before the disposable database
the pinned Auth migrated the environment as its own login
the developer login added triggers to auth.sessions and auth.refresh_tokens
as the superuser, the previous statement let the trigger make the developer login a superuser
as the Auth login, revoke_auth_sessions committed
every session ended and every refresh token revoked
the trigger ran as the Auth login and was refused
rows the tenant holds make it give up within the lock bound
the developer login replaced the trigger with one that lifts the bounds and sleeps at commit
a trigger that lifts the bounds makes the client give up
and the Auth login's server session is ended
the developer login is still not a superuser
